task.description: Independently re-verify ISS-0512's implementation against its validated design and all 4 acceptance criteria.

result.note:
Read ISS-0512.yaml, the validated design (iss0512-async-sandbox-mode-check.md), and ELIXIR-DEV's handoff prose, then independently inspected the full diff (git diff 7dbbbba2..HEAD --stat: exactly 4 changed files -- lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check_async_sandbox_reachability.ex (new, 328 lines), mix.exs (+7), test/mix/tasks/letflow_check_async_sandbox_reachability_test.exs (new, 389 lines), and this run's own step-03-elixir-dev.json handoff -- no unrelated files touched, secrets_test.exs/webhooks_test.exs/tenant_schema_reaper.ex/tenant_template.ex themselves untouched). Ran everything myself (asdf-managed Elixir 1.20.3/OTP 29, added to PATH):

`mix compile --warnings-as-errors` -> exit 0, zero output/warnings.
`mix format --check-formatted` -> exit 0, clean.
`mix test test/mix/tasks/letflow_check_async_sandbox_reachability_test.exs` -> `Result: 16 passed`, 0 failures.
`mix letflow.check_async_sandbox_reachability` (real, unscoped tree) -> `OK -- 66 async:true test file(s) scanned under "test", 2 reach Sandbox.mode/2 (2 permitted, verified exceptions), 0 new violations.` naming exactly test/letflow/secrets_test.exs and test/letflow/webhooks_test.exs -- matches the design's own independently-derived boundary (§1) exactly, and matches ELIXIR-DEV's claimed numbers exactly (not merely trusted -- reproduced).

Design fidelity, verified by direct text comparison, not paraphrase: the async:true anchor regex `^\s*use\s+[A-Za-z0-9_.]+\s*,.*\basync:\s*true\b`, the §3(a) `provisioned_tenant!\s*\(` and §3(b) `(Ecto\.Adapters\.SQL\.)?Sandbox\.mode\s*\(` call-site patterns, and the moduledoc-span/`#`-comment exclusions are byte-identical to the design's specification. The @verified_safe allowlist has exactly the two specified entries (secrets_test.exs, webhooks_test.exs), each citing ISS-0113/ISS-0423, list-of-tuples shape mirroring lint_handoffs.ex's @grandfathered convention. mix.exs wiring: read the alias list directly (lines 91-116) -- "letflow.check_async_sandbox_reachability" sits immediately after "letflow.lint_handoffs" and immediately before "format --check-formatted", exactly the slot the design specifies, with an inline comment stating the placement rationale matching the design's own wording. Style/idiom comparison against lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex (read in full): same module shape (moduledoc contract with 'what this deliberately does NOT check' section, module attributes for constants/allowlists, --dir flag parsing via the identical find_dir_flag/3 clause pattern, guard_empty_scope/2 with the identical empty-scope-is-a-usage-error rule and wording style, pure functions exposed publicly and documented with @spec for direct testability, Mix.raise/1 one-line message shape, '===' rule banners). No deviation in idiom found.

Self-referential-snag trace (not taken on claim): the regression test file itself is test/mix/tasks/letflow_check_async_sandbox_reachability_test.exs, which matches the checker's own test/**/*_test.exs glob and is therefore scanned when the real-tree smoke test runs. Traced its source directly: every synthetic 'use Letflow.DataCase, async: true' / call-site line is a quoted string list element passed to a local `fixture(lines)` helper (line 45: `Enum.join(lines, "\n") <> "\n"`) -- e.g. line 56 reads literally `          "  use Letflow.DataCase, async: true",` on disk, whose first non-whitespace character is `"` (a quote), never the bare token `use`. The anchor regex `^\s*use\s+...` requires `use` to be the line's first non-whitespace token, so no physical source line in this file matches it. The test module itself also declares `use ExUnit.Case, async: false` (line 39), which independently would never satisfy the anchor's `async:\s*true` requirement even if the first-token check were somehow bypassed. Both defenses hold, confirmed by direct inspection of the physical file content, not by re-running the checker against itself in isolation (though the real-tree smoke test's exact-match count of 66, identical to the design's independently-verified figure, is itself indirect proof the file is not miscounted as a 67th async:true file or a spurious violation).

Acceptance-criteria coverage, verified against actual test code (not the handoff's description of it): (a) 'fails the build chain on a genuine violation' -- test 'a violating fixture (async:true + real provisioned_tenant!( call) fails the build' asserts Mix.Error raised with 'found 1 new violation', output containing the fixture path and 'provisioned_tenant'. (b) 'anchoring rejects moduledoc-only mentions' -- two real test cases: 'a moduledoc-only mention of async: true is NOT a real declaration' (async_true_file?/1) and 'a moduledoc mention of provisioned_tenant!/1 in prose is excluded' (real_call_sites/1), both asserting refute/empty-list outcomes against synthetic moduledoc content. (c) 'tenant_schema_reaper.ex/tenant_template.ex-shaped fixtures excluded by file-selection, not a lenient allowlist' -- the 'support-module-shaped files are excluded by file selection' test writes two mode/2-calling .ex (not _test.exs) fixtures into a scratch --dir alongside one harmless *_test.exs file, and asserts the run reports '1 async:true test file(s) scanned' (i.e. the two support-shaped files were never even discovered/counted, proving structural file-selection exclusion rather than allowlist suppression -- the allowlist mechanism is never invoked for these files at all). (d) 'reintroduction of the ISS-0480 shape is genuinely caught' -- same violating-fixture test as (a) is the direct regression proof, distinct from the design's three-layer split (unit/integration/real-tree-smoke), all three of which are present and independently passing.

No idiom or supervision concerns: this is a pure static-text-scanning Mix task, no processes, no supervision tree involvement -- Letflow.InstanceSupervisor and gen_statem idiom questions do not apply. No scope creep: the implementation adds no abstraction beyond what lint_handoffs.ex already established as this codebase's precedent for this exact class of check: it reuses the identical --dir/guard_empty_scope/Mix.raise idiom rather than inventing a new pattern. No type-safety-gap finding to file -- findings maps (%{pattern:, line_number:, line_text:}) are internal to a single-pass static-analysis tool, not application transition logic, so ISS-0512's checker is out of scope for the type-safety observation this gate looks for. Verdict: PASS.
